cards.title: Monte Carlo Integration of Multi-Source Uncertainty
cards.claim: Monte Carlo simulation is an effective method to integrate multiple sources of uncertainty (e.g., clearance prediction error, volume of distribution scaling error, PD potency uncertainty) into a single empirical distribution of the predicted human dose or exposure. This approach handles both closed-form PK/PD models and complex nonlinear models where analytical solutions are unavailable.
conditions: Used when multiple parameter uncertainties need to be propagated simultaneously.
Requires defining distributions for each uncertain input parameter.
required_inputs: Distributions for PK parameters (e.g., log-normal for Vss to avoid negative values).
Distributions for PD parameters (e.g., MIC, potency).
Computational framework for numerical integration or optimization.
limitations: Computational cost increases with model complexity (e.g., ODE integration per sample).
Correlations between parameter uncertainties are often unknown and may be omitted, potentially underestimating combined uncertainty.
cards.downstream_use: Generates empirical distributions of human dose or exposure metrics (e.g., fAUC/MIC) for PTA/CFR analysis.

note: Method/reference scope retained; source identity is available in original evidence.
